---
title: "Multiple outcomes at once"
subtitle: "Build one workbook with every outcome and export it all in a single run"
---

Follow the steps on this page to analyse mortality, recurrence and adverse
events in a single run, and download each kind of plot with every outcome
already inside one ZIP.

It works in these modules: binary outcomes, continuous outcomes, the three
pre-calculated ones, single proportions and single means. Network and
diagnostic accuracy do not have this mode.

## 1. Download the template

1. Open the module you are going to use.
2. In the **Data** step, go to the card on the right, **More than one outcome**.
3. Click **Download XLSX template**, next to the file field.

You get a workbook with three sheets already filled in and in the right format.
Start from that file, not from the template in the left card, which is for a
single outcome and has a different structure.

## 2. Build your workbook

Open the template and follow these rules:

1. **Keep one sheet per outcome.** Add or delete sheets until you have as many
   as you have outcomes.
2. **Rename each sheet with the outcome name.** Write `30-day mortality`, not
   `Sheet1`. That name goes into the plot titles and into the exported file
   names.
3. **Fill each sheet as if it were a separate analysis.** Every study for that
   outcome, with every required column of the module.
4. **Use the same column names in every sheet**, exactly as they appear in the
   template.
5. **Repeat a study in as many sheets as it belongs to.** Sheets do not talk to
   each other: no study is linked to its counterpart in another sheet.
6. Save as `.xlsx`.

::: {.callout-important}
## Sheet name rules
Excel caps sheet names at 31 characters and rejects `:` `\` `/` `?` `*` `[` `]`.
When generating files, MetaVidence replaces anything that is not a letter or a
digit with `_`, so `Progression-free survival` reaches your computer as
`Progression_free_survival`.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Going to use subgroups or meta-regression?
Include the column in **every** sheet where you want that result. If it is
missing from one sheet, that outcome runs without the subgroup and the app
records why, instead of stopping the whole run.
:::

## 3. Upload the workbook

1. Go back to the **More than one outcome** card.
2. Click **Browse** under *Import multi-outcome workbook (.xlsx)*.
3. Pick your file.

Do not use the field in the left card. It reads only the first sheet and treats
the file as a single outcome.

## 4. Check the Data check

The **Data check** card now shows one row per outcome, with the number of
studies found in each.

Read it before moving on. If a sheet has a missing column or an invalid value,
fix the workbook and upload again. That is faster than finding the error after
running everything.

## 5. Set the parameters

Click **Next: parameters**. One thing changes on this screen in batch mode: the
**Outcome name** field disappears, because the sheet name now names each
outcome.

Choose the `sm`, the model and the rest as usual. One single set of parameters
applies to every outcome. Subgroup and meta-regression are not set here: you
pick those columns in step 3, inside the result card, exactly as in
single-outcome mode.

::: {.callout-warning}
## One sm for all
If one outcome needs `RR` and another needs `MD`, do not put both in the same
file. Split them into two workbooks and do two runs.
:::

## 6. Run the analysis

Click **Run analysis**. The app processes each sheet, one at a time, and moves
on to step 3.

## 7. Download the results

In batch mode each result card gains an extra button. For every plot you want:

1. Click **1. Run analysis**, inside the card.
2. Wait for the button beside it to stop showing *2. Download locked*.
3. Click **2. Download**.

The **Subgroup analysis** and **Meta-regression** cards also carry a column
picker. Pick the column there, then click **1. Run analysis** in that same card.
Changing the column locks the download again, so click **1. Run analysis** once
more to rebuild the files for the new column.

Choose the format, the width and the height before downloading, in the fields of
that card. They apply to every outcome in that ZIP.

You get a file named `Forest_Batch.zip`, and inside it one plot per outcome,
with the sheet name in the file name. Repeat for the funnel, the leave-one-out
and whatever else you need.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Prepare only what you will use
Each click on **1. Run analysis** draws that plot for every outcome. With many
outcomes that takes time, so prepare only the cards that go into the paper.
:::
